= GitHub Workflows — what runs, and why some look duplicated

This directory holds the repo's CI/CD. A few workflows *look* like they overlap
but are deliberately distinct — documented here so the apparent duplication is
not "tidied away" into a real coverage gap.

== Hypatia runs in two places (on purpose)

* `hypatia-scan.yml` — the **standalone security scan** (push / PR / weekly).
  Independent; this is the repo's own Hypatia coverage.
* `static-analysis-gate.yml` -> `hypatia-scan` job — runs Hypatia as part of the
  **gate**, then the `deposit-findings` job hands the results to the
  **gitbot-fleet learning** pipeline. This job is also a *required status check*.

Same tool, two different consumers (security scan vs fleet learning). Removing
either loses real function — keep both.

== Secret scanning is single-sourced

`secret-scanner.yml` calls the reusable scanner of
`hyperpolymath/proven-cicd-and-workflows` at a pinned commit (gitleaks, a
Rust-secrets check and a shell-secrets check). An inline TruffleHog job was
removed earlier as redundant with gitleaks; do not add it again.

== Four workflows are self-contained, not reusable callers

`hypatia-scan.yml`, `rust-ci.yml`, `scorecard.yml` and `mirror.yml` follow the
workflows of the estate template (`hyperpolymath/rsr-template-repo`). Earlier each one
called a reusable workflow of the standards repository. Those calls did not
start: the Actions rule of this repository refuses a reusable workflow of a
different owner, and each run failed with no job. Each `uses:` in these four
files is now a step-level action, pinned to a full commit SHA.

`mirror.yml` checks out the full history and prints the commit. It does not
push to another forge: a forge that mirrors this repository must pull from
GitHub. No SSH key secret is passed to a workflow.

`governance.yml` is still a caller of the standards repository (owner
decision, 2026-11-10): the bundle there has 14 jobs, and the template form has
1. It starts only when the Actions rule permits that repository.

== SAST tools are complementary, not redundant

* `codeql.yml` — CodeQL (matrix defaults to `actions`; every repo has workflows).
* `sonarqube.yml` — SonarCloud (shell / JS surface; see `sonar-project.properties`).
* `static-analysis-gate.yml` — panic-attack + Hypatia gate (see above).

Each targets a different language/surface; together they cover what no single
analyser does.
